bootstrap_status.notes: The strict four-dataset cold-item gate is no longer blocked: the approved run full_clean_rebuild_confirmatory_masked_candidate_20260701_20260705 uses 2000 clustered bootstrap replicates, passes the publication gate, and has strict audit approval for the cold-item full-catalog claim only. The separate Video_Games sparse-RRF result remains Video_Games-only local component evidence and does not broaden the approved claim.

official_melt.source_claim: Official PyTorch implementation of MELT: Mutual Enhancement of Long-Tailed User and Item for Sequential Recommendation.
mismatch: Official MELT trains/evaluates chronological sequential recommendation splits, not item-held-out cold full-catalog folds.
Official MELT evaluation uses its own TestData/NegativeSampler candidate protocol, not our full k-core item catalog with user-history masking.

The same-split audit found zero train item-contexts for every strict-fold cold item: Beauty 1,780/1,780 zero-context cold item-folds, Fashion 3,070/3,070, Instruments 11,345/11,345, Books 65,820/65,820.
The current repository's MELT-like evidence is explicitly a proxy and is marked not_official_melt.
official_melt.honest_next_action: Do not treat MELT proxy results as publication-grade. For the approved zero-interaction item-cold claim, record official MELT as documented non-applicable and disclose the rationale instead of reporting a proxy MELT score as official.

tiger_liger_retrieval.source_claim: Official LIGER codebase for Unifying Generative and Dense Retrieval for Sequential Recommendation.
mismatch: The official LIGER pipeline expects its own Hydra dataset preprocessing, semantic-ID generation, sequence generation, and W&B metric logging.

A local export adapter now maps all strict item-held-out folds into LIGER-compatible processed sequence, item-text, embedding, and target-map files; LIGER's own process_data_split parser verified all 100 strict folds.
A smoke evaluation runner uses official LIGER RQ-VAE/TIGER/model_forward/dense-scoring modules and writes canonical JSONL records.
The approved run now includes `tiger_liger_retrieval` full-catalog JSONL records for all four strict datasets, all five seeds, and all 25 seed/fold combinations per dataset.
The existing _bestrec_run TIGER/RQ-VAE code is marked as a proxy or minimal separate benchmark, not mandatory same-split evidence.
tiger_liger_retrieval.honest_next_action: Keep the LIGER/TIGER evidence in the approved cold-item full-catalog gate and preserve the same-split/export audit trail. Do not generalize this evidence to warm-start or broad sequential SOTA claims.

artifact_probe_dry_run.note: Dry run proves the probe itself works before preprocessing; it is not a scored comparator result.

preprocess_audit.runtime_only_repair: Corrected upstream AmazonDataProcessor saved_name from tmp/Video_Games.csv to tmp/Video_Games.csv.gz because the official download URL is a gzip archive; no HSTU-BLaIR source file was edited.

training_audit.compatibility_caveat: Logs show fbgemm dense_to_jagged and jagged_to_padded_dense autograd-kernel warnings under torch==2.8.0+cu128/fbgemm-gpu==1.3.0+cu128; this prevents treating the completed score as faithful upstream publication evidence without further justification.

per_user_export.rank_note: NDCG@10 and HR@10 are exact under upstream top-2500 retrieval because only top-10 membership matters; MRR uses the upstream rank=2501 miss proxy.

strict_hstu_protocol_data.note: These files are not compatible with the already-trained HSTU checkpoint. They are for a future HSTU-compatible retrain with a genuine held-out validation split.

full_dev_epoch1_run.checkpoint_metadata_defect: This one-epoch checkpoint loads but lacks best_epoch metadata; trainer is fixed for future checkpoints.
full_dev_epoch1_run.interpretation: Strict full-scale train/eval/export path works, but one epoch is much weaker than SASRec-SBERT and the HSTU SM120 compatibility reference.

failed_prior_attempt.reason: New checkpoint metadata referenced args.run_id before parser/wrapper exposed it; parser and wrapper are now fixed.

full_dev_epoch10_rerun.interpretation: The strict fair HSTU lane now beats the SASRec-SBERT dev export but remains below the HSTU compatibility reference and upstream report; SOTA remains blocked.

full_dev_epoch30_run.interpretation: The strict fair HSTU lane improves substantially with more training, but held-out test performance remains below the HSTU compatibility reference and upstream report; SOTA remains blocked.

full_dev_epoch60_direct_run.interpretation: The strict fair HSTU lane continues improving with longer training, but held-out test performance remains below the HSTU compatibility reference and upstream report; SOTA remains blocked.

hyperparameter_repair_sweep.experimental_control_note: Earlier dropout-rate runs changed the input preprocessor dropout only; the HSTU encoder linear dropout remained pinned by gin at 0.5. The lab trainer now supports explicit hstu_encoder.linear_dropout_rate and hstu_encoder.attn_dropout_rate overrides and records gin_effective_config.

runs.interpretation: Higher validation but lower held-out test than input-dropout-only 0.3; not selected.
Small weight decay does not beat input-dropout-only 0.3.
Longer training with the best input-dropout setting narrows the gap but still does not beat HSTU-BLaIR evidence.

hyperparameter_repair_sweep.interpretation: The sweep narrows the strict fair HSTU gap but does not close it. SOTA remains blocked under the harsh standard.

strict_hstu_training_lane.caveat: SM120 CUDA 12.8 compatibility lane with fbgemm autograd warnings; full uncapped multi-epoch retrain and canonical per-user export still required before any HSTU-derived publication claim.

union_ltr.selection_protocol: 70/30 validation-user split; train on validation-train users, select on held-out validation-selection users, then evaluate test once.

adaptive_fusion.selection_protocol: 70/30 validation-user split; train user-level confidence/overlap model on validation-train users, select on held-out validation-selection users, retrain on all validation users, then evaluate test once.

item_prior_probe.selection_protocol: 70/30 validation-user split; estimate item target/union appearance prior on validation-train users and select prior beta on held-out validation-selection users.
item_prior_probe.interpretation: Held-out validation selected beta=0, so item-prior calibration did not improve fixed RRF.

content_reranker.selection_protocol: 70/30 validation-user split; add BLaIR profile/content features after translating HSTU histories through recorded user/item maps.
content_reranker.interpretation: Direct candidate-level BLaIR profile features did not beat fixed RRF on held-out validation.

content_adaptive_fusion.selection_protocol: 70/30 validation-user split; add BLaIR profile summaries to user-level adaptive fusion after translating HSTU histories through recorded user/item maps.
content_adaptive_fusion.interpretation: Content-aware adaptive fusion is the strongest development result so far, but the gain over the previous adaptive gate is tiny and it remains below the HSTU comparator.

dev10_resume_finetune.interpretation: Low-LR continuation from dev9 improved validation and HSTU-alone test versus dev9, but validation-selected SASRec fusion is worse than the existing content-aware adaptive best and still below the HSTU comparator.

dev11_temperature_probe.interpretation: Lowering sampled-softmax temperature to 0.03 in the same dropout-0.3 HSTU recipe regressed validation and test performance; this argues against further simple temperature-only repairs.

aborted_branches.dev12_d128: Terminated before completion after smoke success because the first background launch showed impractical runtime/no flushed epoch telemetry; wrapper was then fixed with unbuffered logging.
aborted_branches.dev13_rf_adaptive_fusion: Terminated after high CPU use and no artifact output; histogram-only adaptive fusion completed separately.
aborted_branches.dev13_content_adaptive_histgb: Terminated after 15 minute timeout and no artifact output; no result was produced.

dev13_d96_width_probe.interpretation: Wider d96 HSTU improved validation over prior strict retrains, but the selected checkpoint failed to transfer to held-out test. Validation-selected fixed fusion and histogram adaptive fusion remain below the existing content-aware adaptive best and below the HSTU comparator.

multi_checkpoint_rrf_fusion.protocol: Fixed RRF fusion configs are selected on strict validation records and evaluated once on held-out strict test records. These are development-only because the search was iterated after earlier held-out outcomes were known.

sparse_full_catalog_replay.scoring_definition: Listed component top-50 items receive weighted RRF score; all other unmasked catalog items receive zero; strict sequence history is masked; ties break by ascending BEST-Rec item id.

retired_seed_sets.reason: The development HSTU component runs used seed 20260701 before this sparse-RRF candidate was frozen, so the full previous seed set is retired for this candidate-specific confirmatory run.

publication_blockers: development candidate discovered after iterative held-out feedback
local Video_Games component-comparator gate is not the complete four-dataset publication gate
modern-baseline suite and official-comparator evidence are incomplete for broad publication claims
multi_checkpoint_rrf_fusion.interpretation: Multi-checkpoint RRF fusion is the strongest Video_Games repair so far. The five fresh-seed frozen sparse full-catalog replays improve over every strongest same-seed frozen component, and the aggregate candidate beats the strongest component baseline dev10 with Holm-significant per-user Wilcoxon evidence and a positive user/item/seed-fold clustered bootstrap CI. This is local Video_Games component-comparator evidence only, not a publication/SOTA result.

metadata_repair.note: Older raw SASRec/replay artifacts preserve publication_grade=false, while the provenance manifest records the local confirmatory evidence scope and broad-SOTA blockage.

strict_dev9_validation_safe_fusion.interpretation: Validation-safe fixed top-50 RRF, adaptive fusion, content-aware adaptive fusion, dev10 resumed fine-tuning, dev11 temperature probing, dev13 wider-HSTU probing, and multi-checkpoint RRF improve internal Video_Games metrics over the strict dev9 HSTU retrain. The frozen sparse multi-checkpoint RRF candidate now passes a five-seed local Video_Games component-comparator gate, but broad SOTA remains blocked because this is not the complete four-dataset modern-baseline publication gate.

sasrec_pair_diagnostic.interpretation: SASRec and multiple strict HSTU checkpoints have complementary top-50 hits. The older current-checkpoint diagnostic is not valid for validation-selected fusion because HSTU train targets are effectively BEST-Rec validation targets. The newer strict-dev9 validation-safe fixed fusion, union LTR, adaptive fusion, content-aware adaptive fusion, dev10 resumed fine-tune, dev11 temperature probe, dev13 wider-HSTU probe, and multi-checkpoint RRF still fail to beat the upstream HSTU report, so SOTA remains blocked.

hstu_blair.source_claim: HSTU-BLaIR reports Video Games NDCG@10 = 0.0760 on Amazon Reviews 2023-style data.
mismatch: The Windows Python environment cannot run the upstream stack because HSTU-BLaIR requires Linux-oriented fbgemm_gpu/torchrec/TensorFlow wheels and Linux multiprocessing forkserver.

WSL2 Ubuntu with GPU visibility is available and now has a scripted setup/smoke lane under _bestrec_sota_lab/hstu_blair_wsl; setup uses a clean native WSL clone to avoid mounted-Windows line-ending dirtiness.

The faithful pinned environment installs, but torch==2.2.2+cu121 cannot execute CUDA kernels on this RTX 5060 Ti sm_120 GPU; an explicitly labelled CUDA 12.8 SM120 compatibility port has been added but is not a faithful upstream result until justified.
The preprocess/train stages are now instrumented to record command timing, HSTU-BLaIR artifact hashes/sizes, dataset counts, checkpoint/event-file probes, and parsed upstream eval metrics.
The official preprocessing URL/saved-name pair contains a gzip extension mismatch; the local wrapper repairs this at runtime without editing the external source checkout.

A completed HSTU-BLaIR SM120 compatibility-port score now exists: final full-eval NDCG@10 0.0738224, best full-eval NDCG@10 0.0740335, best epoch/partial NDCG@10 0.0777197. It is stronger than SASRec-SBERT.
A per-user JSONL export now exists for the final epoch under HSTU's one-based item-id convention and upstream top-2500 rank proxy. It matches the TensorBoard final full-eval metrics.

HSTU and BEST-Rec share the same 25,612 Video_Games ASINs and 94,762 raw users, but their item-id and user-id orders differ; the naive item rule bestrec_item_id = hstu_item_id - 1 is false for 25,611 items, and bestrec_user_id = hstu_user_id is false for 94,761 users.

Complete ASIN-based item and raw-user-based user maps, a converted canonical BEST-Rec-id JSONL export, and a converted top-50 teacher JSONL export now exist. The SM120 compatibility caveats still prevent treating the score as faithful pinned upstream publication evidence.

A full single-seed SASRec-SBERT per-user export and paired HSTU/SASRec diagnostic now exist. The diagnostic found two same-user target mismatches and excluded them; on the remaining pairs, SASRec is weaker than HSTU and fixed RRF fusion does not beat HSTU alone.

A split-protocol audit found that HSTU eval targets match BEST-Rec test except two mismatches, while HSTU train targets are effectively BEST-Rec validation targets with six mismatches. This blocks validation-selected HSTU/SASRec fusion with the current HSTU checkpoint.

The strongest development-only sparse local multi-checkpoint RRF candidate now reaches NDCG@10 0.0765298 in the original top-50-union replay and 0.0765303 in the sparse full-catalog replay, beating the upstream HSTU report numerically by about 0.00053, but it was discovered after iterative held-out feedback and has only been frozen as a candidate for fresh confirmatory reruns.

A newer strict-dev9 validation-safe HSTU/SASRec fixed-RRF diagnostic selected HSTU weight 0.85 on validation and reached test NDCG@10 0.0727246, improving strict dev9 but still trailing the local HSTU final export and upstream HSTU report.

Validation-trained artifact-level union LTR and adaptive fusion repairs now exist. The best adaptive fusion reaches test NDCG@10 0.0729497, improving fixed RRF by 0.0002221 but still trailing the local HSTU final export by 0.0008727.
A validation-learned item-prior calibration probe selected beta=0.0 on held-out validation, so it does not improve fixed RRF or adaptive fusion.

Content-aware BLaIR profile reranking and adaptive-fusion probes now exist. The direct content reranker selected fixed RRF; the content-aware adaptive gate reaches test NDCG@10 0.0729567, only 0.000007 above the previous adaptive gate and still below local HSTU by 0.0008657.

A dev10 low-LR continued fine-tune from the dev9 checkpoint reached HSTU-alone test NDCG@10 0.0720203 and validation-selected HSTU/SASRec RRF test NDCG@10 0.0728192, which is worse than the content-aware adaptive best.
A dev11 one-knob temperature probe lowered sampled-softmax temperature to 0.03 and regressed to held-out test NDCG@10 0.0705038, so simple temperature lowering is not a credible path to SOTA.

A dev13 wider-HSTU probe with d=96/dv=dqk=24 improved validation to NDCG@10 0.0801037 but produced held-out test NDCG@10 0.0717703; validation-selected fixed/adaptive fusion reached only about 0.07236, below the current best content-aware adaptive result.

An earlier multi-checkpoint RRF repair over strict HSTU dev5/dev10/dev13 selected weights 0.25/0.25/0.5 with rrf_k=30 and reached held-out test NDCG@10 0.0759152. It is now superseded by the frozen sparse local multi-checkpoint RRF development candidate.
hstu_blair.honest_next_action: Do not claim SOTA from development artifacts. Freeze the sparse local multi-checkpoint RRF candidate exactly, rerun it on fresh confirmatory seeds/splits against the modern comparator suite, and require per-user significance plus bootstrap intervals before any publication claim.
